reason: E1 supports the general principle that ductile, coherent precipitates can strengthen without major ductility loss, but it describes a spinodal nanostructure in a different alloy system, not controlled precipitation in cold-rolled Al0.3CoCrFeNi. E2 confirms that cold rolling and annealing of Al0.3CoCrFeNi can produce precipitates and good strength–ductility balance, but it does not provide evidence for modulus increase, fracture resistance improvement, or the specific strength/ductility targets claimed. The premises on modulus and fracture resistance are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Ductile, coherent, low-misfit precipitates can strengthen without significantly reducing ductility
Cold rolling and annealing of Al0.3CoCrFeNi can produce a high density of nanoscale precipitates
Precipitate–matrix coherence increases effective Young’s modulus
Nanoprecipitates enhance crack arrest and fracture resistance
A 20–30% yield strength increase and >40% elongation are achievable via controlled precipitation
